title: Atlas Approval
description: That a run needed a person's approval, and — if it ever exists — what was approved. Core decides `required` from the task; only a host could ever set the grant fields, and in this version nothing does. Defining this contract grants nothing: Atlas Core is read-only, `ToolGateway` denies every write capability, and no code reads this record to permit anything. What the contract DOES do is make a grant unstateable without saying what it is a grant OF. `granted: true` requires `binds_to`, so an approval can never be a bare boolean that outlives the thing it approved — see docs/safety-model.md, which requires a future approval to bind to the exact diff, command, repository and ref, and to be invalidated when that evidence changes.

required.description: Whether this run may not finish without a person. Derived from the task by `requires_write_approval`, which the producer did not write.

reason.description: Why approval was required. `not_recorded` when the document this was migrated from did not keep one — a plausible sentence here would be indistinguishable from a recorded one.

granted.description: Null means nobody has answered. False means refused. True requires `binds_to`, and nothing in this version can write it.

granted_by.description: Who answered. Null when nobody has.

binds_to.description: What exactly was approved. Required when `granted` is true, because an approval that does not name its subject approves everything. The digest is what makes it expire: if the evidence changes, the approval no longer matches.
